source_scope: The actual Faris pp. 46–47 were visually checked. They explicitly group these children under Robert Barclay Glasgow and Phoebe McFall; Robert’s own dates, two wives and Ohio–Iowa life identify the father account. These exact percentages are subjective assessments of each complete father/profile pair, not statistical measurements.
limitations: This is one retrospective compiled family history. Its list, reported censuses, modern family fields and memorial citations may share evidence; repeated details are not independent proofs. No original birth register, census, Bible or burial record was newly inspected. The 1927 Bible provenance on p. 32 concerns William and Rhoda’s children, not the dates of Robert’s next generation; it is not transferred here. Existing named fathers remain selected. Mothers are separate, ungraded or unselected where previously so. No new parent attachment, merge or live save.

relationship_changes.subject: Glasgow-837
relationship_changes.basis: William Harvey’s full name and both dates, 27 December 1827 and 20 June 1849, match the named child in the printed family list and the existing short-lived Tranquility account. This identifies a child of this particular Robert/Phoebe family without a later adult identity gap.
relationship_changes.limits: The memorial image and original birth/burial records remain uninspected.

relationship_changes.subject: Glasgow-2221
relationship_changes.basis: The printed family list names Elizabeth Patton, born 1830, and her husband William Lowry Cunningham. The distinctive maiden names, year and linked William Cunningham household identify Elizabeth-2221, whose maintained account also cites Faris p. 48 and censuses. The newly inspected page explicitly supplies the paternal family role.
relationship_changes.limits: Page46 does not supply the existing 5 February birth day/month; those fields remain unchanged and are not newly verified. The cited p. 48 and original censuses were not inspected in this batch.

relationship_changes.subject: Glasgow-2222
relationship_changes.basis: The printed list names Rhoda Montgomery, born 31 July 1832, and husband James Fisher Fulton, matching the selected account’s names, full birth date and linked James Fulton. These combined identifiers strengthen the existing Robert father proposal.
relationship_changes.limits: The held memorial citation instead gives Rhoda M. Fulton as 1823–1868. That nine-year disagreement is material: neither birth year nor adult/memorial identity has been resolved. Retain probable 85%, not a confident attachment, and inspect the memorial or age-bearing census next. No birth or death field changes.

relationship_changes.subject: Glasgow-2223
relationship_changes.basis: Faris names Mary Jane as Robert and Phoebe’s child, born 26 May 1835, with first husband Robert Stewart Glasgow and second husband John H. Stewart. The same day/month and distinctive two-husband sequence identify the existing Mary-2223 account despite its 1834 birth year. Taken together these identifiers support confident paternal inference.
relationship_changes.limits: The 1834/1835 birth-year discrepancy remains unresolved and visible. It does not outweigh the full marital identity, but reduces confidence below a near-certain grade. Preserve 1834 in the existing vital field; no source is silently harmonized. The cited p. 89 and original censuses were not newly inspected.

relationship_changes.subject: Glasgow-839
relationship_changes.basis: The family list names Phoebe Ann with the same full birth and death dates, 27 October 1837 and 13 June 1843, as the existing Tranquility child. The named parental family, full name and short lifetime identify this child particularly strongly.
relationship_changes.limits: The Ann name is reported from the family history without changing structured name fields. The memorial image and original birth/burial entries remain uninspected.

relationship_changes.subject: Glasgow-2227
relationship_changes.basis: The printed list names Robert Madison, born 16 April 1840 and died 29 January 1865 at Vicksburg, Mississippi. These exact dates, middle name and unusual death setting match Robert-2227’s military-hospital account. The same page reports Robert M. in Robert B.’s 1850 household, cohering with its explicit child list.
relationship_changes.limits: The household and list are statements in one compilation, not independent inspected census and military proofs. The original 1850 census, Roll of Honor and memorial images remain uninspected; no military or vital field is changed.

relationship_changes.subject: Glasgow-840
relationship_changes.basis: Nancy Emeline’s full name and exact dates, 2 June 1843 and 5 March 1849, match the printed child list and existing short-lived Tranquility account. This specific family and lifetime identify her as the listed Robert/Phoebe child.
relationship_changes.limits: The profile retains Ohio as birthplace, whereas the book’s narrative reports Indiana for Nancy and Susanna. That reported place discrepancy remains open; no birthplace field changes. Original birth and burial records remain uninspected.

relationship_changes.subject: Glasgow-841
relationship_changes.basis: Faris calls this child Sarah Margaret, born 6 November 1845, and names husband John M. Lytle. The exact date, Margaret name and linked John Lytle household identify the existing Margaret-841 account. Its female structured field and marital account also show that the biography’s male pronouns are an editorial error.
relationship_changes.limits: Report the fuller Sarah Margaret name in the biography without changing structured name fields. Correct the male pronouns in the complete proposed draft. No birth, death or mother field changes; original records remain uninspected.

relationship_changes.subject: Glasgow-2228
relationship_changes.basis: The printed family list names Susanna Rachel, born 5 July 1847 and died 5 May 1861 in Iowa, exactly matching this child’s maintained dates, middle name and death setting. The same account places Susanna in the reported 1850 and 1860 Robert households. This coherent identity supports the explicit paternal role.
relationship_changes.limits: The book’s narrative reports Indiana as the birthplace of Susanna and Nancy, while this profile retains Ohio. Leave that place discrepancy open. The reported censuses are not independently inspected records, and no vital field changes.
